target.title: [codex] Reduce idle cost scan CPU
target.body:
## Summary

- resolve models.dev pricing once per Codex project-rollup build instead of once per cached usage row
- carry a fresh native cost-cache timestamp through startup hydration so the existing one-hour token TTL suppresses the redundant follow-up scan
- keep stale caches, managed Codex homes, and Pi-backed cache hydration eligible for normal refreshes
- add deterministic performance and fresh/stale hydration regression coverage

## Root cause

The project-rollup path rebuilt a report for every cached session file without forwarding a resolved pricing catalog. Each row therefore fell back through the models.dev cache path and repeated filesystem metadata work. Startup then hydrated the same fresh cache and later scheduled another full token-cost aggregation because hydration did not restore the existing refresh TTL state.

## Performance proof

- Time Profiler on current `main`: cost-history scanning, project aggregation, and repeated `ModelsDevCache.fileMetadata` dominated the idle-startup trace
- real unchanged 30-day local Codex corpus, bundled release CLI: 57.05s wall / 37.97s CPU before; 15.88s wall / 12.12s CPU after
- exact packaged app: accumulated CPU reached 15.07s by 25s and stayed at 15.07s through 99s and 15.08s through 141s; the previous delayed second scan added about 13s CPU
- final 60s idle Time Profiler trace contained only nine one-sample app frames and no cost-scanner frames

## Validation

- `make check`
- `make test` — all 48 shards passed
- `swift test --filter 'CostUsageScannerBreakdownTests|CostUsageFetcherCacheSnapshotTests|CostUsagePerformanceGateTests'` — 63 tests passed
- `swift test --filter UsageStoreCachedTokenHydrationTests` — fresh and stale cache behavior passed
- `./Scripts/package_app.sh` — exact release app packaged and launched
- source-blind packaged-app/CLI contract — idle CPU plateau, valid nonempty daily/project JSON, stable historical digest, monotonic active-day totals
- structured autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings, 0.82 correctness confidence
